newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SIA says other alliances possible.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SIA says other alliances possible.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) chief executive officer Cheong Choong Kong said on Tuesday the Singapore flag carrier would consider further airline alliances.

"Is there any chance of us creating other alliances with other airlines? Yes, there is always that possibility," Cheong said in response to a question after a speech to the Aviation Club Press Club of Australia.

"I think I would be dishonest if I was to say that our alliance with Swissair, Delta has been spectacularly successful both that alliance has given us benefits and we are better off by having that alliance."
"The scenario is constantly shifting so anything is possible," Cheong said.
Cheong said airline alliances were one of the more notable phenomena sweeping the aviation industry.
He said that at May 1996, there were 389 airline alliances worldwide. He added these alliances are constantly changing.
"Like a promiscuous lover, airlines are not adverse to jumping in bed to bed if they think there are more exciting times to be had," he said.

Cheong said he could not comment on speculation that SIA was planning to buy Qantas Airways Ltd's 19.4 percent stake in Air New Zealand Ltd or whether Singapore would seek an alliance with Air New Zealand or with its associate Ansett Airlines Ltd.
Air New Zealand earlier on Tuesday announced an alliance with United Airlines.
